samples.summary: PDF export is the one color sink left un-normalized by this change — `styleColor()` still accepts only `#RRGGBB` and returns BLACK for everything else
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-style-map.ts:143-153` — `styleColor()` runs `defaultColorResolver` then `/^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/`, falling back to `{r:0,g:0,b:0}`. After this change the canvas painters treat the legacy `''` reset as unset (theme default), and DOCX/PPTX normalize `rgb(...)`/`#RGB` through `toRgbHexColor`, but the PDF backend was not updated. Its callers are `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:389`, `:635`, `:706` (run text) and `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-table-painter.ts:178` (cell background). Consequences: (a) a run cleared with the legacy `''` prints black in PDF instead of the theme default the canvas now paints (visibly wrong in the dark theme where `Theme.defaultColor` is the light ink); (b) an HTML-pasted `rgb(255, 0, 0)` run — the routine shape per `view/clipboard.ts:150` — prints black in PDF while DOCX/PPTX now emit `FF0000`; (c) a pasted `rgb(...)` table cell background prints as a solid black cell via `pdf-table-painter.ts:178`. The fix belongs on `styleColor` (delegate to the new shared `toRgbHexColor`), not on the diff.

samples.summary: PPTX export gains its first runtime (value) import of `@wafflebase/docs` on a path documented as DOM-free / Node-safe
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:3` adds `import { toRgbHexColor } from '@wafflebase/docs'` — previously this module imported only types from docs (erased at compile time). `packages/slides/src/node.ts:170-172` documents `exportPptx` as "DOM-free; safe for Node consumers without a polyfill", and `packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:1` imports it via `@wafflebase/slides/node`. Under plain Node resolution the docs `exports["."]` "node" condition (`packages/docs/package.json:15-21`) maps to `dist/node.js`, which the diff correctly extends (`packages/docs/src/node.ts:100`), so the common path is fine. The residual risk is any consumer that resolves `@wafflebase/docs` to the browser entry (`src/index.ts`) in a Node/SSR context — e.g. the slides vitest alias at `packages/slides/vite.config.ts:17` — which now loads the full DOM-shaped docs entry as part of PPTX export. Importing from `@wafflebase/docs/node` in this module would remove the ambiguity. I could not confirm a resolver that actually breaks, hence low confidence.

samples.summary: `resolveStoredColor` — the guard that makes the `''` reset behave as unset — is not exported from either package entry, so out-of-package color resolvers cannot apply it
samples.evidence: The diff exports `toRgbHexColor` from both `packages/docs/src/index.ts:69` and `packages/docs/src/node.ts:100`, but `resolveStoredColor` stays module-private. Consumers that resolve docs `StoredColor` values outside docs' painters — e.g. `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:52` (`makeColorResolver`, which maps `null/undefined` to the deck theme text color but returns `''` verbatim for the legacy reset) — have no way to reuse the guard if they ever paint outside `paintLayout`. Today every slides paint path funnels through `paintLayout`/`resolveColorAtPosition`, which now normalize, so nothing is broken; this is a consistency/reachability gap, not a live defect.
searchedFor: read packages/docs/src/index.ts and packages/docs/src/node.ts export lists
grep fillStyle =|strokeStyle = in packages/docs/src and packages/slides/src/view/canvas

finding.summary: PPTX export still writes arbitrary docs color strings into `<a:srgbClr val>`; the same untrusted, non-hex values this delta now normalizes on the DOCX side (rgb()/rgba() from HTML paste) produce an invalid ST_HexColorRGB deck.
finding.evidence: This delta added `toDocxHexColor` because `InlineStyle.color` can hold non-hex CSS (`packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:151` and `:154` copy `el.style.color` / `el.style.backgroundColor` verbatim, i.e. `rgb(255, 0, 0)`). Slide text boxes edit the SAME docs model through the docs `TextEditor` (`packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:46,666`, which routes paste through `parseHtmlToBlocks` at `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1117`). On PPTX export the value goes `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:277` → `storedColorToThemeColor` (`:185` → `colorFromStringOrTheme`) → `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:36`, which only strips a leading `#`, upper-cases and XML-escapes: the emitted attribute becomes `<a:srgbClr val="RGB(255, 0, 0)"/>`. Same for `backgroundColor` (`:284`), `underlineColor` (`:291`) and `marker.color` (`:134`). The new `hasColor` guard only rejects `''`, so this sink is left with the exact class of defect the docs sibling just fixed.

verdict.reason: The claimed unnormalized PPTX color sink does not exist. `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:3` imports `toRgbHexColor` from `@wafflebase/docs`, and the single bridge `storedColorToThemeColor` (`text.ts:183-200`) normalizes every concrete color through it at `:188-189` (`const hex = toRgbHexColor(...); return hex ? colorFromStringOrTheme('#'+hex) : undefined`), dropping anything not expressible as six hex digits; its role arm is validated against `ROLE_TO_SCHEME` at `:192`. All four sinks the finding names go through that bridge: `marker.color` (`:135`), `s.color` (`:281`), `s.backgroundColor` (`:287`), `s.underlineColor` (`:293`). So `colorFromStringOrTheme`/`color.ts:36` never receives a raw docs model string on this path, and `rgb(255, 0, 0)` from HTML paste becomes `FF0000` (`packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:106-113`) or is dropped; `toRgbHexColor` returns only `[0-9A-F]{6}` or `undefined` (`color.ts:89-116`). The finding's `hasColor` guard is absent from src (grep hits only under `.agent-review/` artifacts), and its cited line numbers do not match (`text.ts:277` is the `sz=` font-size attribute; `:284` is a comment). A grep of `srgbClr|solidFill` across `packages/slides/src/export` shows no other emission fed from the docs `InlineStyle` model.

finding.summary: The new `hasColor` guard only recognizes the string form of the legacy cleared color; the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` shape the docs model explicitly documents as reachable still reaches `<a:srgbClr val=""/>`.
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:40-43` (the counterpart fix in this PR) states that a cleared color can also arrive as "an `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` shape". `hasColor` (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:180`) tests only `c != null && c !== ''`, so that object passes, `storedColorToThemeColor` returns it unchanged (`:186`), and `colorChildXml` (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:36`) emits `<a:srgbClr val=""/>` — precisely the invalid ST_HexColorRGB the guard's own doc comment says PowerPoint rejects. Fix belongs on the new guard (or, better, on `colorChildXml` so every caller is covered).

verdict.reason: The finding describes a `hasColor` guard testing only `c != null && c !== ''`, but no `hasColor` symbol exists anywhere in the repository (Grep over all *.ts: no matches), and text.ts:180 is a doc-comment line, not that test. The real bridge, `storedColorToThemeColor` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:183-200), does not return the value unchanged: lines 187-189 fold both the bare-string and the `{kind:'srgb'}` arms into one branch and normalize through `toRgbHexColor`, returning `undefined` unless the result is six hex digits. `toRgbHexColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:89-90) returns `undefined` for any falsy input, so `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` yields `undefined`; the callers' truthiness checks (text.ts:136, 282, 288, 294) then omit the color child, so `colorChildXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:35-36) is never reached with an empty value and `<a:srgbClr val=""/>` cannot be emitted on this path. The comment at text.ts:170-175 names that exact shape as one the normalizer drops. Every other `colorChildXml` call site in packages/slides/src (color.ts:40,53; effects.ts:22) takes an already-typed `ThemeColor`, and `storedColorToThemeColor` is the only StoredColor bridge, so there is no alternate unnormalized entry point either.
